nextStoryContext: US-004 added a new '## Security' section to README.md, inserted between the '## Architecture' section's closing '---' rule and '## Recent changes' (i.e. right before 'Recent changes', after 'Architecture'). The section is one self-contained paragraph: it names the actual default ('permission_mode = "bypassPermissions"', citing DEFAULT_PERMISSION_MODE in src/config/permission-mode.ts, applied when ~/.config/cam/config.toml is missing or the key is unset -- exactly what cam init writes on a fresh machine), states the consequence in plain terms (every worker/orchestrator session runs with no permission prompt: full read/write/exec reach of the operator's account, unprompted, per edit/command), frames it explicitly as a deliberate autonomous-looping trade-off rather than an oversight (so it reads as honest disclosure, not an apology), and names the mitigation by its real config key: '[loop] worker_isolation = "container"' in scripts/cam/project.toml (default 'host'), which routes worker sessions into container isolation. Did NOT add a --permission-mode CLI flag anywhere (that invariant is untouched) and did NOT alter README lines 155-158 (the existing 'permission mode is read from ~/.config/cam/config.toml, no subcommand exposes a flag' sentence), which the new section complements rather than duplicates. File grew from 329 to 347 lines (net +18), satisfying the AC6 'not truncated, length >= main' oracle. All 9 acceptance-criteria oracles (including the 3 grep-based ones plus typecheck/tests/check:all) were verified green before commit; the reviewer-judgment oracle (AC5, an honest self-contained disclosure paragraph) was self-assessed at Layer A but the reviewer's independent Layer B run is the artifact of record.
